lines: Fortes creantur fortibus, & bonis,
Eſt in iuuencis, eſt in equis patrum
Virtus. nec imbellem feroces
Progenerant, aquilæ columbam {k}.
Iuſques à voir la poſterité, porter ores les nerfs, ores
les cicatrices, ores quelconques autres marques de ſes
anceſtres, & de ſon origine, teſmoins les Lepides Ro-
mains, deſquels y en eut trois d'vne maiſon, ayant cha-
cun l'œil couuert d'vne petite peau. Et Nice Bizantin,
qui naſquit noir comme vn more, rapportant pluſtoſt
ſon ayeul, que ſa mere belle & blanche, engendrée tou-
tesfois, par adultere, d'vn Ethiopien {l}. Mais les forces de
la nature, ni des races, ne peuuent pas tant, que nous ne
voyons quelquefois la poſterité degenerer, & diſſembla
ble à ſes progeniteurs: cõme des beaux, naiſtre des laids
& difformes: des robuſtes & forts, iſſir des impuiſſans,
& foibles: des bons & vertueux, proceder des vicieux, &
meſchans {m}. Autrement, ſi par fois, cela n'aduenoit ain-
ſi faudroit pour le bien public defendre par loy gene-
rale & inuiolable, aux laids, debiles, & meſchans, le ma-
riage, & compagnie charnelle des femmes: afin que tous
infalliblement, naſquiſſent beaux, puiſſans, & robuſtes.
Sur quoy Alexandre Aphrodiſée, ſe trauaille fort à ſon-
der, & monſtrer la cauſe, pour laquelle on voit aduenir
ſouuent, qu'vn homme ſtupide, groſſier, & ſot, voire vn
nyés, produira des enfans accors, prudẽs, ſages, & diſcrets
Et conclud la raiſon eſtre, pour autant qu'vn badaut, en
l'acte venerien, ſe laiſſe tellement ſurmonter, & vaincre
à la volupté preſente, qu'il ne penſe lors à autre choſe:
ayant volontairement plongé l'eſprit, & l'ame dans le
corps, dont la ſemence eſt puiſée & tirée de ce corps
parmy lequel l'eſprit ſe trouue, participe grandement
de la vertu raiſonnable: & fait que les enfans, qui en
deſcendent, ſont plus prudens, & ſpirituels que le pere.
Comme au contraire, ceux qui ſont ingenieux, diſcrets,
ou ſçauans, par ce que leur eſprit inceſſammẽt trauaille,
& ſ'occupe ailleurs qu'au plaiſir de la chair: voire meſ-
mes ſur l'inſtãt de l'acte, auquel du tout ne ſe laiſſe vain

uncertain.note: four lines of italic Latin verse (Horace, Odes IV.4) set as a quotation; transcribed as a paragraph block per §6, not as headings. The marker k is a superscript italic k after 'columbam', with the point following it. p014 ends with a full stop, so continues_prev is false; the quotation ends with a point, so continues_next is false. The body paragraph 'Iuſques' is indented and is a new paragraph.
the mark after 'Virtus' is a round dot on the baseline with no tail (3x): a point, set tight against 'nec' and normalized per §1.

uncertain.text: qui naſquit noir comme vn more, rapportant pluſtoſt
uncertain.note: the fourth letter of 'pluſtoſt' is an ascender-height stroke with only a faint top hook and no left nub (6x), taller than the t beside it; it lacks the crossbar of a t. Read ſ from the word (pluſtoſt = plustost); a reader could take it for 'pluttoſt' or 'plultoſt'.

uncertain.text: nyés, produira des enfans accors, prudẽs, ſages, & diſcrets
uncertain.note: the mark after 'prudẽs' is a round dot at the baseline with a detached comma-tail below it (6x). Read as a comma (worn sort, and the list continues 'ſages, & diſcrets'), but the two-piece shape could be a semicolon set low. No mark at all is printed after the final 'diſcrets' (line end); the sentence continues with a capital 'Et' on the next line.
final mark after 'robuſtes' is a round dot on the baseline (4x): a point, and 'Sur' follows with a capital.

uncertain.text: mes ſur l'inſtãt de l'acte, auquel du tout ne ſe laiſſe vain
uncertain.note: the last word 'vain' is broken at the line end with no hyphen (vain-cre continues on p016); its final letter is heavily inked, read n by width. continues_next true.

every double s on the page was checked at 3x-4x: diſſembla (lines[9]), iſſir and impuiſſans (lines[11]), naſquiſſent and puiſſans (lines[17]), groſſier (lines[20], heavily inked), laiſſe (lines[23] and lines[33]), inceſſammẽt (lines[31]) all show two ascender-height strokes, i.e. the ſſ ligature; no ſs was found.

spacing: the compositor sets many commas and colons tight ('origine,teſmoins', 'mains,deſquels', 'ayeul,que', 'tesfois,par', 'nature,ni', 'degenerer,&', 'progeniteurs:cõme', 'beaux,naiſtre', 'forts,iſſir', 'vertueux,proceder', 'vicieux,&', 'inuiolable,aux', 'riage,&', 'femmes:afin', 'infalliblement,naſquiſſent', 'der,&', 'ſouuent,qu'vn', 'nyés,produira', 'venerien,ſe', 'ingenieux,diſcrets', 'ſçauans,par', 'l'acte,auquel') and some with a space before ('nerfs ,', 'anceſtres ,', 'maiſon ,', 'more ,', 'blanche ,', 'tant ,', 'cauſe ,', 'ſtupide ,', 'puiſſans ,', 'corps ,', 'chair :', 'peau .'). All normalized per §1.

line breaks without a hyphen, transcribed as printed: lines[9] 'diſſembla' + lines[10] 'ble'; lines[33] 'vain' + p016. Hyphens are printed at 'Ro-', 'cha-', 'tou-', 'ain-', 'gene-', 'ma-', 'ſon-', 'meſ-'.

the key letter printed before 'Horace' is a large italic swash K that reads as a capital, while the body marker after 'columbam' is a small superscript k. Keyed k (lowercase, continuing p014's g, h, i). The book numeral on the second line is 'iij.' (i + ij ligature with two dots, 6x); Horace's ode is in book IV, but the print reads iij and is kept as printed. Note is set beside body lines 0-2, below the verse.
'vij' is set with the italic swash v; the ij ligature carries its two dots. Points after 'vij', 'c' and 'xij' are all printed.

note m is set beside body lines 14-17 ('ſi faudroit' to 'infalliblement'), three lines below its marker in lines[13]; the margin was free there. 'au v.' uses the swash italic v; 'placitis' is printed with a round final s; 'ſophor.' with long s.
spaced capitals, closed up per §3; ends with a point.
